title: Boundary region map file
overview: bcRegionMapFile selects the case-relative file that stores the mapping between boundary-region names and integer region identifiers.
principle: The default is grid/bcRegionMap.txt. Grid generation writes this file under the mesh-output root; solver boundary-data loading reads it under the mesh-input root or the selected source Case directory.
architecture: GridConfig::GetBcRegionMapFileName reads the optional string parameter and applies the default only when the key is absent or empty. GridConfig carries the resolved path into grid generation. BcData resolves the same configured path for runtime reads. A present parameter with a non-string type is rejected.

proves: The parameter has a default path and is consumed by both grid-map generation and solver map loading.
does_not_prove: The contents of the map are physically or numerically validated.
Every grid input format provides equivalent boundary-region semantics.

verification.scope: The integration test configures a non-default map path, checks that conversion writes it, then runs the production simulation path that reads it. CI execution is tracked separately.

examples.title: Default and case-specific map location
examples.input: bcRegionMapFile is absent, or is set to results/bcRegionMap.txt.
examples.calculation: When absent or empty, GridConfig resolves grid/bcRegionMap.txt. When set, grid generation resolves the configured path under the mesh-output root and BcData resolves it under the mesh-input root or source Case.
examples.result: The producer and solver use one shared path contract; the STL-to-Gmsh pipeline explicitly selects results/bcRegionMap.txt to preserve its sidecar layout.
examples.limitations: This controls file location only. It does not validate region-name semantics, boundary-condition physics, or solver support for each region.

caveats: The path is relative to the active mesh input or output root unless the path itself is absolute.
A configured path does not prove that the map contents match the selected grid or boundary-condition model.
